item.title: Shinshu Miso: Japan's Most Widely Produced Miso — Guide
item.description: Shinshu miso, the rice-based miso produced in Nagano, is Japan’s most widely made variety, accounting for around half of all the country’s miso production, thanks to the region’s cool climate being ideal for the slow fermentation that gives it its characteristic golden colour and balanced, medium-salty flavour. Beyond seasoning countless dishes, the miso can be explored at breweries around the prefecture, some historic and centuries old, which offer tours, tastings and shops explaining the fermentation process behind this staple of Japanese cooking.

item.title: Shinshu Soba & Nagano Food Guide: What to Eat in the Japan Alps
item.description: Nagano Prefecture has one of the most distinctive regional food traditions in Japan — shaped by a landlocked mountain climate, heavy snowfall, intense cold, and the need to preserve food through long winters. The absence of a coastline drove the development of an extraordinary preserved-food culture: lacto-fermented vegetables (tsukemono), long-aged miso from locally grown soybean and barley, smoke-dried mountain trout and carp, dried mushrooms and wild vegetables gathered from the alpine forests.
